For Petitioner : Ms. Nivetha Bernice  ORDER

A private complaint alleging that the seethana articles returned back to the wife through the respondent Ramesh her Tata Ace vehicle driver not been properly delivered and therefore, he must be prosecuted for the offence under Sections 406 of IPC is a criminal breach of trust and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 420 of IPC came to be considered by the learned Judicial Magistrate and found that it is a bereft of details of any commission of cognizable offense and dismissed.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has preferred revision before the Sessions Court.
The learned Sessions Judge, after going through the records, concurred the view expressed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate and dismissed the revision.
Being aggrieved by the concurrent finding, the present Original Petition is filed.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner states that only when the wife filed M.C.No.124 of 2014, he came to know that the seethana articles sent through the respondent herein not taken delivery by his wife.

When the respondent has informed the petitioner that all the seethana articles loaded in his vehicle were unloaded in the door steps of his wife's house , he believed it but only when M.C.No.124 of 2014 came for consideration he realized that the articles were not delivered to his wife.
Even assuming that the allegations made in complaint is true.

The complaint filed after nine years of the occurrence necessarily need to be rejected at the outset, the learned Judicial Magistrate has rightly rejected and the Sessions Court also dismissed the revision petition.
There is n o s c o p e t o i n t e r f e r e t h e c o n s i d e r e d o r d e r o f t h e C o u r t s b e l o w e x e r c i s i n g https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
Hence, this Criminal Original Petition is dismissed.
The Inspector of Police, All Women Police Station(W8), Thirumangalam, Chennai District.
